items.title: How one German city is preparing for climate extremes
items.description: Western Europe has recorded its hottest-ever June and July, and extreme weather from wildfires to storms is here to stay. How can we adapt to what seems to be the new normal? Cities like Kiel are trying new ideas.

items.title: Turkey MPs back historic law on reintegrating PKK militants
items.description: Turkey's parliament has taken a major step toward ending four decades of conflict with the PKK. The new law sets out how some militants can return to civilian life, but leaves Abdullah Ocalan's future unresolved.

items.title: Russia: Top court bans opposition anti-war party from vote
items.description: Yabloko, Russia's only anti-war party, has been barred from September's parliamentary elections. The motion to bar Yabloko was filed by the nationalist pro-Kremlin party Rodina.

items.title: New train service connects Finland and Sweden for first time in decades
items.description: The service will enable rail travel from Portugal to Lapland - what is believed to be the longest train journey in Europe.
